headline: Phillies now eight days into offseason after Wild Card exit
recap: The Phillies have not played since October 1, when their season ended in Atlanta with a 6-2 loss in the decisive Game 3 of the NL Wild Card Series -- eight days ago now, not fresh news. Michael Harris II's three-run homer in the bottom of the first put starter Aaron Nola and the Phillies in an early hole; he was pulled after 1 2/3 innings with all three runs charged to him. Zack Wheeler relieved and allowed a two-run homer to Ozzie Albies in the fourth. Philadelphia's only runs came on Alec Bohm's sixth-inning groundout, which scored Kyle Schwarber, and Trea Turner's eighth-inning sacrifice fly, which scored Derek Hill. Matt Olson's solo homer off Jonathan Bowlan in the seventh rounded out Atlanta's scoring. Grant Holmes got the win in relief for Atlanta; Nola took the loss.

Philadelphia finished the regular season 88-74, second in the NL East, six games behind the division-winning Braves. The Phillies reached the postseason as the wild card and were eliminated 2-1 in the best-of-three Wild Card Series, falling in Game 3 after splitting the first two games, both also played in Atlanta.

There is no next game: the Phillies' season remains over. Atlanta's season is over too: the Dodgers closed out the NLDS in four games, winning Game 4 on the road Wednesday 4-1. The Dodgers have not yet begun the NLCS.
